disposition: Generator defects are fixed in build_manifest.py and the manifest is rebuilt from the sealed lane record; every other finding is published as a per-row citation_review overlay on the manifest (never a hand edit of generated text) so downstream rows and the handbook cite only rows whose citations were verified.

findings.claim: The headroom row's evidence[2] says the pin_behind_upstream status was 'refuted by adversarial verification', which contradicts the row's own review_status (pin_behind_upstream), the row's own upstream block, and the sealed lane record.
findings.evidence: Manifest JSON pointer /foundation/9/components/2: review_status='pin_behind_upstream' (line 2199), upstream.latest='v0.38.0' (2189), evidence[2]='pin_behind_upstream proposed by foundation lane, refuted by adversarial verification' (2204). In <host-path> there are TWO headroom pin_behind_upstream proposals: lanes[2] ('beyond') proposals[10] has survives=true, verification='survived'; lanes[0] ('foundation') proposals[11] has survives=false but its claim text is a PROVENANCE dismissal ('a maintenance item, not a review finding') and its votes[1] states verbatim 'Direction: refuted=true means the dismissal ... does not hold; the pin_behind_upstream status itself is CONFIRMED by live and snapshot evidence.' github-freshness.json repositories['https://github.com/headroomlabs-ai/headroom'].latest_release = {tag v0.38.0, 2026-09-21T23:48:52Z} vs pin 0.37.0. The identical phrasing on instructions-skills/skills-ref (line ~600s) and workers/codex-for-claude (line ~763) accompanies a status that WAS changed to confirmed_default, so on headroom the same sentence asserts the opposite of the row it sits in.
findings.fix: In the dated review artifact, record that the headroom evidence line must read that the foundation lane's *dismissal* was refuted and the pin_behind_upstream status survived in the beyond lane; cite lanes.json lanes[2].proposals[10] (survives=true) rather than the refuted foundation proposal.

findings.claim: Six in-scope rows carry the thinner 'beyond'-lane entry and silently drop the foundation lane's better-cited entry for the same layer/component; the manifest states no merge rule for the two lanes.
findings.evidence: lanes.json foundation-lane selected entries exist for token-efficiency/headroom (evidence includes 'docs/token-efficiency-stack.md L37 (Default ledger: 0 calls / 0 saved ... 9,616->2,128 upstream estimated tokens, 7,488 saved; exact recovery and restart passed.)' and 'docs/full-stack-convergence.md L145'), workers/claude-code (evidence includes 'docs/foundation-closure-20260921.md L92-95'), isolation/worktrunk ('docs/foundation-closure-20260921.md L55'), isolation/sandbox-runtime ('docs/full-stack-convergence.md L50'), durable-memory/ai-memory ('docs/foundation-closure-20260921.md L58', gh api receipt, 'star-candidates.json: 8 memory repositories dispositioned alternative'). The manifest instead reproduces the beyond-lane rows verbatim, whose evidence is only redacted '<host-path>' pointers: lines 2202-2203 (headroom), 1690-1697 area (durable-memory/ai-memory), 1012 (sandbox-runtime), 1035 (isolation/worktrunk), 718 (workers/claude-code), 2179 (token-efficiency/context-mode). manifest.method.review names only 'review lanes from a lanes.json record ... every proposed change adversarially verified' and defines no lane-precedence rule.
findings.fix: Record in the review artifact that the generator must either merge both lanes' evidence[] for a duplicated layer/component or state and apply an explicit lane-precedence rule; as generated, six rows lost durable repo-relative citations that exist in the sealed record.

findings.claim: Four evidence JSON pointers into github-freshness.json do not resolve: they append the release-tag/tree path to the repository key, but those four repositories are keyed at repository root.
findings.evidence: Unresolvable pointers: line 294 'github-freshness.json#/repositories/https:~1~1github.com~1tobi~1qmd~1releases~1tag~1v2.8.3'; line 318 '...~1rtk-ai~1rtk~1releases~1tag~1v0.49.0'; line 760 '...~1openai~1codex-plugin-cc~1tree~1v1.0.6'; line 1170 '...~1DeusData~1codebase-memory-mcp~1releases~1tag~1v0.11.0'. In <host-path> the existing keys are exactly 'https://github.com/tobi/qmd', 'https://github.com/rtk-ai/rtk', 'https://github.com/openai/codex-plugin-cc', 'https://github.com/DeusData/codebase-memory-mcp' (469 keys scanned; no tag/tree variant present). The manifest's own lane_limits.foundation names this key-shape hazard for a different set ('ast-grep, mcporter, difftastic, agent-browser and shellcheck are keyed ... by their full release/tree URLs, not by repository root'), and those five do resolve — these four are the inverse error.
findings.fix: Record that these four evidence strings should point at the repository-root keys; the underlying freshness data exists and the manifest's upstream blocks already reflect it, so only the citation string is wrong.

findings.claim: At least eight evidence citations name the wrong line in a repo-relative doc; the quoted text exists but at a different line, so the citation as written does not resolve.
findings.evidence: Verified against the worktree copies. (1) line 376 cites 'docs/foundation-closure-20260921.md L20 (ECC row ...)' — L20 is the table separator '| --- | --- | --- |'; the ECC row with pin 2b6e8397 is L21. (2) line 539 cites 'docs/foundation-closure-20260921.md L21 (Shan row, reviewed pin bde3f031)' — L21 is the ECC row; the Shan row is L22. (3) line 2095 cites 'docs/foundation-closure-20260921.md L59 (Bounded discovery, extraction and browser operations. Search acceptance does not qualify every crawl/research mode.)' — L59 is the Durable memory row; that Web research text is L60. (4) line 1473 cites 'docs/full-stack-convergence.md L53 (Scoped QMD BM25 search then get | Current useful hits; zero vectors is intentional)' — that row is L52; L53 is Semantic RAG. findings.claim: Seven why_selected strings assert execution evidence (receipts, captured test output, measured runs) while no evidence[] item is a receipt path — and the manifest's own lane_limits records that no receipt was opened.
findings.evidence: Rows and assertions: line 812 workers/worktrunk 'a behaviour receipt, not just a version bump' (evidence: foundation-layers.json pointer + docs/full-stack-convergence.md L124-129); line 1282 code-navigation/repomix 'that wave attached captured upstream test output (a selected subset passed)' (evidence: doc only); line 1035 isolation/worktrunk 'the layer's evidence (worktrunk-list, token-native-retained-functional-20260920) is native receipt on this stack' (evidence: two '<host-path>' strings); line 1690 durable-memory/ai-memory 'the only candidate the project has native receipts for across both Codex and Claude ... (native-memory-lifecycle-20260919, wsl-memory-maintenance-20260920)' (evidence: three '<host-path>' strings); line 2206 token-efficiency/headroom 'Retained ... on its existing native evidence (native-headroom-mcp-20260920)'; line 2049 web-research/openresearch 'one of the four selected upgrades in the 2026-09-21 wave with captured upstream test output'; token-efficiency/rtk why_selected 'the project already ran the comparison ... a measured, retained counterexample' where the only measured doc line cited (docs/full-stack-convergence.md L139-141) reports a different number (RTK shared project estimate 2,337 -> 2,371), not the pilot. The manifest's lane_limits.foundation states verbatim: 'I did not read the referenced evidence receipts (evidence/receipts/*.json, evidence/artifacts/*) or blueprints/convergence-practice/*; every accepted_within_scope status below is documented-as-done ..., NOT observed-now by me.'
findings.fix: Record that these seven why_selected strings are documented-as-done, not receipt-backed; either add the concrete receipt path (the repository does carry evidence/artifacts/full-stack-convergence-20260921/, referenced at docs/full-stack-convergence.md L132) or relabel the wording to 'documented' in the follow-up artifact.

findings.claim: comparison_that_would_overturn contains a prescriptive demotion recommendation conditioned on an unverified hypothesis, which is promotion/demotion by review rather than an overturn condition.
findings.evidence: Line 1404: '... If its curated index has drifted behind the libraries actually queried - the likely consequence of 114 days without a push - this should be demoted to keep_but_compare against direct primary-documentation fetch ...'. The antecedent ('has drifted') was not tested: the row's evidence[] is foundation-layers.json#/layers/5/components, a gh api metadata call, and docs/foundation-closure-20260921.md L57 — none of which queries the curated index. The manifest's own critic.next_steps entry for foundation/document-retrieval instead asks only to 'Write one dated maintenance note for context-hub ... stating whether the sole curated-documentation component stays and what observation would trigger a replacement search.'
findings.fix: Record that this sentence should be restated as the overturn condition only (a named documentation query where context-hub returns a stale page and direct primary fetch returns the current one), with the 'should be demoted' recommendation removed from the generated field.

findings.claim: why_selected misreads the file it cites: star-candidates.json records beads as a candidate disposition, not as an adoption, so 'i.e. already promoted into the catalog' is a promotion statement not supported by the citation.
findings.evidence: Line 694: 'It is also carried in star-candidates.json as a targeted_candidate for agent-task-state, i.e. already promoted into the catalog.' The cited entry in <host-path> reads {"repository":"https://github.com/gastownhall/beads","decision":"targeted_candidate","layers":["agent-task-state"],"rationale":"Could provide structured ready/blocked work beyond durable prose memory; evaluate as task state rather than a competing market-data or ..."} — an explicit 'evaluate', not an adoption. The actual adoption lives elsewhere (foundation-layers.json layers[2].decisions[2] dependency-task-queue, selection=conditional), and lanes.json lane_limits.beyond states the two demotion_proposed entries 'propose retiring a stale star-audit candidate label on components the catalog has already adopted'.
findings.fix: Record that the gloss should cite foundation-layers.json layers[2].decisions[2] for the adoption and describe the star-candidates row as a stale candidate label, not as evidence of promotion.

findings.claim: Both jcodemunch-mcp rows are held at confirmed_conditional with no mention of the contrary disposition recorded in the same sealed input set (obsolete_or_ineligible, with a licensing blocker).
findings.evidence: Manifest code-navigation/jcodemunch-mcp (evidence at line 1193, review_status confirmed_conditional, review_note null) and token-efficiency/jcodemunch-mcp (evidence at line 2227, same status). star-candidates.json records {"repository":"https://github.com/jgravelle/jcodemunch-mcp","decision":"obsolete_or_ineligible","layers":["code-retrieval"],"rationale":"Overlaps accepted code retrieval and its current Dual-Use License requires resolution for a commercial-trading project; publisher savings and aggregate counters are not local proof.","license":"jCodeMunch-MCP Dual-Use License 1.1 (2026-06-30)"}. Neither row's evidence[] cites star-candidates.json and neither why_selected addresses the license condition. By contrast the sibling token-efficiency/ccusage row (line 2155) does cite star-candidates.json for its alternatives.
findings.fix: Record the unresolved contradiction as a keep-but-compare/licence-reconciliation item naming star-candidates.json, rather than leaving two confirmed_conditional rows silent about it. Do not change the status by review.

findings.claim: Nineteen evidence entries are the bare placeholder '<host-path>' with no pointer, and one of them redacts a session scratchpad path that no longer exists, so the citation is unverifiable by construction.
findings.evidence: Bare '"<host-path>"' evidence items occur at manifest lines 846, 1049, 1880, 1921, 1961, 2179, 4940, 5474, 6321, 6346, 6396, 6556, 6674, 6699, 6724, 6749, 6774, 6799, 7617 (221 lines in the file contain the placeholder). The same scratchpad-path class backs the surviving moai-adk candidate proposal in lanes.json.
findings.fix: Record that session-scratchpad artifacts are not durable evidence: either the awesome-list sweep output must be retained under evidence/ and cited by repo-relative path, or the claim should be marked unverifiable. findings.claim: Two comparison_that_would_overturn values name no fixture path, runnable command or measurable metric.
findings.evidence: Line 1012 isolation/sandbox-runtime: 'A task where a per-command restriction is insufficient and a whole-agent boundary is required.' — no fixture, command or metric; the same row's why_selected admits 'I did not re-fetch its upstream metadata'. The foundation lane's own entry for the same component (lanes.json, lane 'foundation', isolation/sandbox-runtime) offers a concrete alternative: 'An actual filesystem/HTTP boundary test where a command escapes the configured policy', which the manifest dropped. Line 989 isolation/apple-container: 'Nothing on this host - it is a Mac-only recipe. A WSL/Linux container persistence requirement would be a different decision, not an overturn of this one.' — states no falsifier at all.

findings.claim: Two claude-code rows make star-audit and candidate-sweep claims without citing star-candidates.json (or any source) in evidence[].

findings.claim: A refuted unmaintained_signal is rewritten to review_status "confirmed_default", promoting a component whose governing decision is selection "conditional". This is promotion by review, which the practice forbids.
findings.evidence: build_manifest.py:451-457 maps a refuted status change to `confirmed_default` for status_value in ("demotion_proposed", "unmaintained_signal"). Sealed record: <host-path> lanes[foundation].result.layers[quality-evaluation].selected[skills-ref].status == "unmaintained_signal" (its own why_selected in the instructions-skills row reads "Signal, not a demotion"). The only decision carrying skills-ref in this layer is foundation-layers.json#/layers/10/decisions/0 portable-skill-reference with "selection":"conditional","review_status":"accepted_within_scope"; the same holds at #/layers/1. Published row: catalogs/sota-convergence/manifest-20260922.json:2550 "review_status": "confirmed_default". The manifest's own usage elsewhere ties confirmed_default to a selection:"default" decision (git-github-automation/worktrunk, owned-worktrees selection "default"). The adjacent branch at build_manifest.py:458-464 states the hazard verbatim: "never treat this as a completed refutation -- that would silently upgrade an unreviewed status (e.g. \"unmaintained_signal\") to \"confirmed_default\"", but guards only survives=None.
findings.fix: On survives=False, restore the class the row would carry absent the signal: derive it from the governing decision's selection (confirmed_default only when selection=="default", otherwise confirmed_conditional), or emit a neutral "confirmed_signal_refuted". Regenerate; the in-scope row quality-evaluation/skills-ref should read confirmed_conditional. Same defect also produces instructions-skills/skills-ref (manifest line 545) and workers/codex-for-claude (line 741).

findings.claim: The same component is published with two contradictory review classes on identical upstream facts: demoted to unmaintained_signal here, and confirmed_default in the workers layer, because the adversarial refutation is matched per layer rather than per repository.
findings.evidence: manifest-20260922.json:3969 git-github-automation/codex-for-claude "review_status": "unmaintained_signal" with why_selected (line 3975) asserting the staleness signal "no upstream push since 2026-07-08 (76 days)". manifest-20260922.json:741 workers/codex-for-claude, same repository and the same upstream block (pushed_at 2026-07-08, stars 33467), carries "review_status": "confirmed_default" plus evidence line "unmaintained_signal proposed by foundation lane, refuted by adversarial verification". lanes.json lanes[foundation].proposals[4] is kind=unmaintained_signal, layer="workers", repository=https://github.com/openai/codex-plugin-cc/tree/v1.0.6, survives=false, verification="refuted" (votes refuted flags false,true). No equivalent proposal exists for layer git-github-automation, so the identical signal stands unrefuted there. Net effect: a demotion the record's own adversarial verification rejected for the same repository is still published.
findings.fix: Key unmaintained_signal/demotion verdicts by repository (or propagate a repository-level refutation to every layer row for that repository) in build_manifest.py's verdict lookup, then regenerate so both codex-for-claude rows carry the same class. Combined with finding 1, that class should be the decision-derived one (companion-backend is selection "optional", review_status partial_acceptance), not confirmed_default.

findings.claim: The row's only citation is an unresolvable redaction placeholder, and the generator discarded a foundation-lane row for the same component/layer that carried two openable, verified citations.
findings.evidence: manifest-20260922.json:2486-2488 evidence == ["<host-path> -> layers[quality-evaluation].decisions[deterministic-quality-tools] and components[promptfoo]"] - a single entry with no repo-relative path, no JSON pointer and no receipt. lanes.json holds two rows for this component/layer: lanes[beyond] (the one published, same evidence and why text) and lanes[foundation].result.layers[quality-evaluation].selected[promptfoo] with evidence ["foundation-layers.json#/layers/10/decisions/1 (deterministic-quality-tools, conditional)", "docs/foundation-closure-20260921.md L62 ('Behavior oracles and independent findings. Consensus and synthetic fixtures alone are insufficient.')"]. I verified both of those: layer 10 decision 1 is deterministic-quality-tools, selection "conditional", component_ids include promptfoo; docs/foundation-closure-20260921.md L62 contains that sentence verbatim. Separately, why_selected (line 2489) states "I did not re-fetch promptfoo's upstream metadata this pass" while the row still publishes a full upstream block and pin_behind_upstream=false with no freshness citation (the values do match github-freshness.json).
findings.fix: When a component/layer pair appears in more than one lane, prefer (or merge) the row whose evidence[] contains resolvable citations; for this row restore the foundation-lane evidence pair and add "github-freshness.json#/repositories/https:~1~1github.com~1promptfoo~1promptfoo" to support the published upstream block.

findings.claim: Zero verifiable citations: one redacted host path plus an uncited gh graphql result, while the discarded foundation-lane row carried two openable citations. The claimed steveyegge -> gastownhall rename is not corroborated by any retained artifact.

findings.claim: comparison_that_would_overturn is unfalsifiable: it states that nothing would overturn the selection and pre-judges the only named comparison. Same pattern at line 3460 for observation-inference/claude-hud.
findings.evidence: manifest-20260922.json:2448 (playwright-test): "Nothing about the runner itself; the separation would be overturned only by collapsing the two, which would weaken the gate." - names no fixture path, no runnable command and no metric, and rules the comparison out in advance. manifest-20260922.json:3460 (claude-hud): "Nothing about accounting; a rendering failure would be a display bug. findings.fix: Replace both with a runnable comparison: for playwright-test, a named browser-gate spec that the locked runner and an interactive playwright-cli session produce different verdicts on; for claude-hud, a rerun of the recorded terminal-resume procedure in evidence/artifacts/full-stack-convergence-20260921/hud-observation.json that fails to render. hosting-services/nextjs ("An application requirement the locked stack cannot meet. findings.claim: Row execution-broker/alpaca-py (the execution card) carries the DATA card's why_selected, comparison_that_would_overturn and evidence[]; the lane's execution-role rationale, overturn and note are absent from the manifest entirely.
findings.evidence: manifest-20260922.json:5759 why_selected = "Same repository as the execution card, retained separately for the data role because the broad-universe collection (24,310,292 bars per adjustment) was run on it..." — byte-identical to row data-alpaca-py at :5785. Its overturn (:5760) is a data-coverage criterion ("An entitled provider (Databento or Massive...) delivering pre-2016 or pre-2020-delisting daily bars"), which cannot overturn a broker-SDK selection. Its evidence (:5755-5756) cites "#/layers/market-data-reference/0" and the redacted pointer resolves to <host-path>#/layers/execution-broker/3, which is the data-alpaca-py card (role "Official Alpaca historical/streaming data and paper-trading SDK"); the alpaca-py card is index 2 (role "Official Python Trading API and market-data SDK"). The sealed lane record lanes.json (trading lane, execution-broker) carries a distinct selected item catalog_id=alpaca-py with why_selected "Confirmed because the selected Alpaca path in runtime-target.json is explicitly the official SDK at 0.44.0, and the executed paper receipt was produced on it...", overturn "...measured on the same 27 local lifecycle cases", evidence [trading-by-layer.json#/layers/execution-broker/2, github-freshness head 232179c1, runtime-target.json#/broker_boundaries/1/selected_path] and a note about duplicate identity. None of those strings occur in the manifest (checked: "the executed paper receipt was produced on it" false, "232179c1" false, "Card appears twice" false), and review_note is null at :5753. Root cause: tools/sota-convergence/build_manifest.py:444 keys the merged lane state as (layer_id, selected["repository"]), so two catalog components sharing one repository in the same layer collide and the later item silently overwrites the earlier; lanes.json "lost" is an empty array and no collision is recorded.
findings.fix: Key merge_lanes' status map by the lane item's catalog_id (falling back to repository) instead of repository alone at build_manifest.py:444, and raise/record a reconciliation entry when two selected items collide on the same key. Add a regression test with two same-repository components in one layer (none exists: tests/test_sota_convergence.py has no duplicate/collision case). Regenerate; do not hand-edit the manifest.

findings.claim: sanitize() swallows the JSON pointer attached to a host path, so 64 of the 90 file citations in the 58 reviewed rows (affecting 50 of 58 rows) publish as bare "<host-path>" with no locator, even though the pointer carries no private information.
findings.evidence: HOST_PATH_PATTERNS at build_manifest.py:345 is re.compile(r"/home/[^\s\"']+"); '#' is not excluded from the character class, so "<host-path>#/layers/market-data-reference/3 (decision=default...)" becomes "<host-path> (decision=default...)". The asymmetry is visible in the published output at manifest-20260922.json:4719, where an unattached pointer on the same line survives: "<host-path> and #/layers/data-quality-orchestration/4 (decision=default, evidence_level=source_review)". 92 of the 97 evidence strings in the 58 rows are "<host-path>" forms; 16 of the 90 file citations point inside the catalog repository itself and could be emitted repo-relative without redaction at all.
findings.fix: Split each citation on '#' and redact only the path component (or add '#' to the excluded class), so "<host-path>#/layers/execution-broker/2" is published; rewrite citations under the catalog repository root to repo-relative paths before sanitizing; emit a stable token (e.g. "<lane-state>/trading-by-layer.json#/...") for the private state directory. Add a sanitize test asserting a JSON pointer survives (tests/test_sota_convergence.py:239 currently only asserts the path is removed).

findings.claim: The README's "Optional lane fields carried, never invented" bullet documents the exact behaviour prior finding 1 required be removed, and names a constant that does not exist in the code.
findings.evidence: README.md:163-176 reads: "**Optional lane fields carried, never invented** (`merge_lanes`, `OPTIONAL_SELECTED_FIELDS`): a lane's `selected[]` item may set `why_selected`, `comparison_that_would_overturn`, `role`, `upstream_now` and/or `catalog_pin`; ... so `build_manifest()` can carry them onto every merged row that key can land on -- a foundation `components[]` row, a trading `entries[]` row, or a `lane_groupings[].selected` row." The implementation does the opposite for the first two row kinds: build_manifest.py:423 `ROW_LANE_FIELDS = ("why_selected", "comparison_that_would_overturn")`, applied at build_manifest.py:638-640 (foundation components) and :665-667 (trading entries), so role/upstream_now/catalog_pin are deliberately kept off those rows (build_manifest.py:414-421 comment). `grep -rn OPTIONAL_SELECTED_FIELDS .` returns exactly one hit: README.md:164 — the symbol exists nowhere in build_manifest.py. The README also omits `catalog_id`, which the code and LaneItemPlacementTests treat as a first-class carried field, and this bullet still describes the fields as landing on `status[(layer_id, repository)]` directly rather than on `status[key]["lane_item"]` (build_manifest.py:479-481).
findings.fix: Rewrite README.md:163-176 to match ROW_LANE_FIELDS: merge_lanes puts every non-merged selected[] field into `status[key]["lane_item"]` generically (no whitelist); foundation `components[]` and trading `entries[]` rows take only `why_selected`/`comparison_that_would_overturn` (they keep the baseline pin/upstream); `lane_groupings[].selected` rows take the whole `lane_item` verbatim (role, catalog_id, catalog_pin, upstream_now, and any future field). Replace the `OPTIONAL_SELECTED_FIELDS` reference with `MERGED_SELECTED_KEYS` / `ROW_LANE_FIELDS` / `lane_item`.

findings.claim: The new regression note's pre-fix figures are attributed, in the present tense, to a repository path that holds a different file at both the base and the head commit, so the claim is not reproducible and reads as false to anyone who checks it.
findings.evidence: README.md:268-277 says "the pre-fix working-tree manifest at `catalogs/sota-convergence/manifest-20260922.json` (itself a pre-fix run against that same work-dir) has 15 trading rows (three of them the non-taxonomy `awesome-list-convergence`/`star-audit-targeted-candidates`/`unmaintained-reference-material` ids) and `candidates_total=18`". Parsing that path at both revisions: at d093a4c it has 12 trading rows, no non-taxonomy ids, `foundation_layers=16`, `candidates_total=34`, and no `lane_groupings` key at all; at e3c9470 it has 12 trading rows, `foundation_layers=20`, `candidates_total=16`, `lane_groupings=3`, `lane_grouping_candidates=2`. The post-fix half of the note therefore checks out exactly against e3c9470; the pre-fix half (15 rows / candidates_total=18) corresponds to an uncommitted working-tree state that exists in neither commit and cannot be recovered (the branch has a single commit on d093a4c).
findings.fix: Rephrase the second bullet in past tense and name the artifact that actually carried the pre-fix numbers (e.g. "an uncommitted pre-fix regeneration of the manifest, not preserved in git, reported 15 trading rows and candidates_total=18"), or drop the unreproducible pre-fix figures and keep only the post-fix numbers, which are verifiable from the committed manifest at this commit.

findings.claim: A sibling assertion was not migrated to the new `lane_item` shape and is now vacuous: it can no longer fail regardless of merge_lanes' behaviour.
findings.evidence: tests/test_sota_convergence.py:502-503 read `self.assertNotIn("why_selected", status_absent[key]["lane_item"])` / `self.assertNotIn("comparison_that_would_overturn", status_absent[key])`. The diff updated only the first line (`-        self.assertNotIn("why_selected", status_absent[key])` / `+ ...["lane_item"])`). Under the new implementation `status[key]` top-level keys are always exactly {status, evidence, note, lane, lane_item} (build_manifest.py:473-481), so line 503 asserts the absence of a key that can never be present — it would still pass if merge_lanes invented `comparison_that_would_overturn` inside `lane_item`, which is the never-invented contract this test exists to guard.
findings.fix: Change line 503 to `self.assertNotIn("comparison_that_would_overturn", status_absent[key]["lane_item"])`.

findings.claim: Prior finding 1's foundation half is untested: no assertion checks that role/catalog_id/catalog_pin/upstream_now stay off a foundation `components[]` row.
findings.evidence: `LaneItemPlacementTests.test_taxonomy_row_takes_only_row_lane_fields` (tests/test_sota_convergence.py:1474-1483) exercises only `manifest["trading"]` (`rows["layer-z"]["entries"][0]`). The inherited fixture's only foundation layer is `{"layer_id": "found-a", "title": "Found A", "components": []}` (tests/test_sota_convergence.py:1147-1149), so the foundation branch of the same filter (build_manifest.py:638-640) is never executed with a lane item carrying those fields. The code is correct by inspection and the real manifest at e3c9470 shows zero leakage onto foundation rows, but nothing guards a regression on that path.

findings.claim: `counts.lane_groupings_note` names only two of the counts that are scoped to foundation[]+trading[]; `components_confirmed` and `pins_behind_upstream*` have the same scoping and also silently exclude `lane_groupings[].selected` rows.
findings.evidence: build_manifest.py:780-784 states "candidates_total and candidates_by_disposition stay scoped to foundation[] and trading[] rows and never include them". But `all_rows = manifest["foundation"] + manifest["trading"]` (build_manifest.py:743) also drives `components_confirmed` (:760-764) and `pins_behind_upstream` / `pins_behind_upstream_unique_components` (:748-751, :765-767). A `lane_groupings[].selected` row with a `confirmed_*` status would therefore not be counted in `components_confirmed`, and that scoping is undocumented. In the committed e3c9470 manifest the 23 lane_groupings selected rows are all `keep_but_compare`/`demotion_proposed`/`unmaintained_signal`, so there is no live discrepancy today — this is latent.
findings.fix: Extend `lane_groupings_note` to say that every foundation/trading-scoped count (candidates_total, candidates_by_disposition, components_confirmed, pins_behind_upstream, pins_behind_upstream_unique_components) excludes lane_groupings rows, or add an explicit `lane_grouping_selected` count alongside `lane_grouping_candidates`.
